findings.description: Allotment = max allotment minus 30% of net income. Code: snap_max_allotment - snap_expected_contribution (net*0.3, rounded), floored by snap_min_allotment.
findings.evidence: check.py TX size-3 2026-01, 19 net-income values 0..5000, model == exact-fraction oracle in all cases (mismatches 0); e.g. N=1000 -> 485, N=1667 -> 284, N=2500 -> 35.

findings.description: State chooses to round 30% up (1) or round the allotment down (2); the statute says round down. Code applies (1) for all states. With a whole-dollar max allotment (785), M-ceil(x)=floor(M-x), so all options give identical results.
findings.evidence: Both oracles matched in all 19 cases; ceil(round(n*0.3,2)) vs exact ceil(3n/10) for n=0..20000: 0 mismatches.

findings.description: Minimum benefit applies only to 1-2 person households; the code gives min allotment 0 for size 3 (DC/MD/NJ overrides don't apply to TX).
findings.evidence: snap_min_allotment=0.0 in all cases; repo tests passed.

findings.description: Deny vs suspend is a State choice for a 3+ household with no benefits; the benefit is $0 either way, and the model returns 0 (never negative).
Initial-month proration and the <$10 rule don't apply in a non-initial month; the full allotment is issued.
findings.evidence: No proration in the code; N=1 -> 784.

findings.description: The input net income is rounded half-up (option A) for all states; the State may use its TANF procedure (B). The allotment-step equivalence holds either way.
Conforms assuming no 271.7 reduction order applied in Jan 2026 (not verifiable from the pinned sources).
EA (off since 2023-03) and the DC-only benefit are 0 for TX Jan 2026, so snap == normal allotment.

limitations: Net income and eligibility were injected directly; max allotment values and Texas's actual State-option elections were not verified; 271.7 reduction status assumed none; non-integer net income was only reasoned about; only selected repo tests were run.
